name: Frontline Medic
oracle_text:
Battalion — Whenever this creature and at least two other creatures attack, creatures you control gain indestructible until end of turn.
Sacrifice this creature: Counter target spell with {X} in its mana cost unless its controller pays {3}.
blocked_sentences: Sacrifice this creature: Counter target spell with {X} in its mana cost unless its controller pays {3}.

needs.what: A selector key that asks whether an object's **printed mana cost contains an {X} symbol** -- e.g. `{"has_x": true}` (and its negation) added to `SELECTOR_KEYS` and matched in `selectors.matches` as `ctx.state.card_of(obj).mana_cost.x_count > 0`. The data already exists and is parsed: `ManaCost.x_count` (mana.py:68, incremented at mana.py:90 for each `{X}` token), so this is a filter clause over an existing field, not a new characteristic. It must be legal inside a `TargetModel.selector` on a `kind: "spell"` target, which is where every card of this shape reads it ("target spell with {X} in its mana cost", "target creature spell with {X} in its mana cost").
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `mana_value` is the only cost reader in `SELECTOR_KEYS` and it is a numeric comparison through `_compare` against `card.mana_value` (selectors.py:495-498). `ManaCost.mana_value` counts X as 0 by default (mana.py:110-116), so an X spell is indistinguishable from the same cost without the X: Fireball `{X}{R}` and Shock `{R}` are both mana value 1, and a `mana_value` clause therefore either catches both or neither. `mana_symbols` is the DSL's only symbol-level cost reader and cannot stand in twice over: it is a `value_keys` entry rather than a selector key, so it cannot filter a pool at all, and `validate_mana_symbols` (values.py:370-374) requires `of` to be one of W/U/B/R/G -- there is no spelling for X, by design, since it was built for chroma. Nor can the restriction be moved off the selector and into a condition: `TargetModel` (schema.py:74-93) carries only `selector`, `count`, `one_per_player` and `optional`, with no condition slot, and an activated ability's own `condition` is checked by legality before targets are chosen so it cannot see the spell either. Every remaining route is an approximation that changes which spells the ability may point at.

needs.what: A player spec that names **the controller of a targeted spell**, so "unless its controller pays {N}" can charge the right seat -- e.g. `{"controller_of_target": "t1"}` in `selectors.select_players`, resolved as `[state.stack_item(sid).controller for sid in ctx.target_sids("t1")]`. With it, the whole family writes itself with existing vocabulary: `{"op": "may", "player": {"controller_of_target": "t1"}, "pay": {"mana": "{3}"}, "else": [{"op": "counter", "target": "t1"}]}`. The same key also unblocks "target spell's controller" on non-counter cards ("unless that spell's controller pays", "that spell's controller discards a card"), and the authoring queue holds dozens of `Counter target spell unless its controller pays {N}` printings waiting on exactly this one clause.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The unless-pays *shape* already ships -- `may` with `pay` plus `else` is precisely it, and the loader documents that reading at loader.py:1659-1668 (Rhystic Study) -- but it can only bill a player some **trigger binding** already names. `select_players` (selectors.py:604-641) offers `{"controller_of": <binding>}`, which reads `ctx.bindings` and nothing else; bindings are written by `triggers.event_bindings` (triggers.py:394-397) and by `snapshot`, and an activated ability's StackItem carries no binding for the targets it was activated with (stack.py:622-631 passes `targets` and `bindings` as separate things). This is why ward could be written and a targeted counterspell cannot: ward's payer arrives as `controller_of: subject` off a `becomes_target` event. `{"target": "t1"}` is the obvious substitute and silently does the wrong thing: it routes to `ctx.target_players`, which keeps only refs of kind `"player"` (context.py:55-56), and a spell target is kind `"stack"` (context.py:58-59) -- so it returns `[]` and `op_may` falls back to `chooser = ctx.controller` (ops_control.py:57-58), asking Frontline Medic's own controller to pay {3} to counter the spell they just targeted. `{"controller_of": ...}` cannot be fed from the target either: `resolve_pool`'s `{"target": ...}` form seeds from `target_oids`, also object-kind only (selectors.py:165-172), so neither a selector nor a `snapshot` can reach the targeted spell to bind it. `player: "opponent"` is the tempting approximation and is refused: the targeted spell's controller is not necessarily an opponent, and with two of them `select_players` hands `op_may` a list whose first entry is an arbitrary seat.
